name: Account Closure Process
description: The formal operational procedure for closing customer accounts at FirstUK Bank. The process is managed by the Operations and Retail Banking departments and is intended for use by Branch Staff, Operations, and Customer Service.

name: Head of Operations
description: The individual responsible for the ownership and ultimate oversight of the Account Closure SOP document.

name: Branch Staff
description: One of the primary audience groups responsible for executing the account closure procedure within a branch environment.
context: Audience | Branch Staff, Operations, Customer Service

name: Operations
description: The departmental team responsible for the operational execution and management of the account closure workflow.
context: Audience | Branch Staff, Operations, Customer Service

name: Customer Service
description: Staff members responsible for interacting with customers and facilitating the account closure process.
context: Audience | Branch Staff, Operations, Customer Service

name: Customer Account Closure Process
description: A standardized operational procedure for closing bank accounts, including SmartSaver, Current, and Mortgage accounts. The process covers both customer-initiated requests and bank-initiated closures resulting from fraud, regulatory concerns, or policy violations.
context: Establish standardized procedures for closing customer accounts (SmartSaver, Current, Mortgage)
through customer-initiated requests or bank-initiated closures due to policy violations, regulatory concerns, or fraud.

name: SmartSaver Account
description: A specific banking product subject to the account closure procedures outlined in this SOP.

name: Current Account
description: A specific banking product subject to the account closure procedures outlined in this SOP.

name: Mortgage Account
description: A specific banking product subject to the account closure procedures outlined in this SOP.

name: Closing Account
description: A customer account being closed through either a customer-initiated request or a bank-initiated action due to compliance or policy issues.
context: bank-initiated closures due to policy violations, regulatory concerns, or fraud.

name: Account Closure Process
description: The end-to-end operational procedure for closing bank accounts. It covers both customer-initiated and bank-initiated closures across all product types and delivery channels.

name: Savings Account
description: A banking product type subject to the account closure process.

name: Current Account
description: A banking product type subject to the account closure process.

name: Mortgage Account
description: A banking product type subject to the account closure process.

name: Account Closure Process
description: The end-to-end operational workflow for closing a customer account. It involves identity verification, balance calculation, handling of payment mandates, and archiving. Timelines vary between 3–5 business days for customer-initiated requests and immediate action for bank-initiated closures.
context: Timeline: 3–5 business days (customer-initiated), Immediate (bank-initiated with notice)

name: Closure Request Receipt
description: The initial stage of the process where the request to close the account is first received.

name: Customer Identity Verification
description: A step to verify the identity of the customer requesting the closure before proceeding with the workflow.

name: Final Balance Calculation
description: The action of determining the final outstanding balance on the account to be closed.

name: Payment Mandate Processing
description: The stage where active standing orders and direct debits associated with the account are processed or cancelled.

name: Closure Type Assessment
description: A branching point to determine if the closure is customer-initiated or bank-initiated. Customer-initiated requests follow the normal path, while bank-initiated requests trigger a requirement to investigate and document the reason.

name: Final Balance Transfer
description: The action of transferring or remitting the remaining final balance to the customer.

name: Closure Confirmation Issuance
description: The step of providing the customer with formal confirmation that the account has been closed.

name: Records Archiving
description: The mandatory retention step where account records are archived for a period of 6 years.

name: System Account Status Update
description: The final administrative action of marking the account as 'Closed' within the bank's core system.

name: Account Closure Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for closing a customer account, initiated via branch, phone, online, or mail. It involves request reception, identity verification, and confirmation of account status before proceeding with closure.

name: Closure Request Reception
description: The initial stage where a customer request to close an account is received through one of four approved channels. The actor must collect the account number, full name, address, reason for closure, and preferred final payment method.
context: Request Channels: Branch: In-person request to manager, Phone: Call customer service, Online: Submit closure form, Mail: Written request

name: Request Recording
description: The action of logging the closure request details, including the date, time, method of request, and the customer's contact information.
context: Record request (date, time, method, customer contact info)

name: Customer Identity Verification
description: The process of confirming the requester's identity using either security questions or the verification of official documents.
context: Verify customer identity (security questions or document verification)

name: Account Hold Confirmation
description: A check to ensure the account is not subject to any freezes, disputes, or active fraud investigations that would prevent closure.
context: Confirm no holds on account (freezes, disputes, fraud investigation)

name: Closure Implications Briefing
description: The act of informing the customer that once closed, no further transactions can occur, interest accrual stops, and records will be archived.
context: Explain closure implications (no further transactions, interest stops, records archived)

name: Branch Manager
description: The staff member responsible for receiving in-person account closure requests at the branch level.

name: Customer Service
description: The team responsible for handling account closure requests received via the phone channel (0800-555-2265).

name: Customer
description: The individual initiating the account closure request through one of the bank's approved channels.

name: Account Hold Gate
description: A decision point to determine if the account has freezes, disputes, or fraud investigations. If holds exist, the closure process cannot proceed normally.
context: Confirm no holds on account (freezes, disputes, fraud investigation)

name: Closing Account
description: The specific bank account that is the subject of the closure request and verification process.

name: Bank-Initiated Closure Process
description: An operational workflow for closing customer accounts triggered by regulatory reasons, fraud, policy violations, or dormancy. The process typically requires a 30-day notice period, unless an emergency closure is triggered.

name: Emergency Bank-Initiated Closure Process
description: An accelerated closure workflow used when fraud or security risks are confirmed. It involves an immediate account freeze and closure within 7 days, with same-day customer notification.
context: Immediate account freeze (if fraud/security risk confirmed)

name: Manager
description: An authorized actor capable of initiating the bank-initiated account closure process.

name: Compliance Head
description: An authorized actor capable of initiating the bank-initiated account closure process, specifically for regulatory or compliance-related triggers.

name: Closure Initiation Step
description: The initial action where a Manager or Compliance Head triggers the account closure workflow.

name: Reason Documentation Step
description: The requirement to record the specific trigger for closure (regulatory, fraud, or policy) within the bank's system.
context: 2. Document reason in system (regulatory, fraud, policy)

name: Closure Notice Preparation Step
description: The preparation of a formal notice to the customer, adhering to a 30-day notice requirement unless the situation is an emergency.
context: 3. Prepare notice to customer (30-day notice required, except emergencies)

name: Customer Notification Step
description: The final step of sending a letter to the customer explaining the reason for the account closure.

name: Immediate Account Freeze Step
description: An immediate action taken in emergency scenarios to freeze the account when fraud or security risks are confirmed.
context: Immediate account freeze (if fraud/security risk confirmed)

name: Closure Trigger Decision
description: The determination of whether an account should be closed based on regulatory reasons, fraud, policy violations, or dormancy.
context: Regulatory Reason: Compliance violation, AML breach, regulatory order
Fraud: Account used fraudulently, customer identity issue, unauthorized access
Policy Violation: Breach of terms & conditions, customer misconduct
Dormancy: No activity + failed contact attempts

name: Emergency vs Standard Closure Gate
description: A decision point to determine if the closure is an emergency (fraud/security risk), which bypasses the 30-day notice period for an immediate freeze.
context: Immediate account freeze (if fraud/security risk confirmed)

name: Regulatory and AML Compliance Check
description: A mandatory check for compliance violations or AML breaches that serves as a trigger for bank-initiated closure.
context: Regulatory Reason: Compliance violation, AML breach, regulatory order

name: Target Account
description: The customer account subject to the bank-initiated closure process, which may be frozen or closed.

name: Affected Customer
description: The customer whose account is being closed by the bank and who must be notified of the reason.

name: Account Verification Process
description: An operational procedure to verify the status, ownership, and legal standing of an account before further actions are taken. The process typically concludes on the same day.

name: Account Status and Ownership Verification
description: A series of checks to ensure the account exists, is active, and that the ownership matches the customer's identity.
context: Account exists and is active (not already closed)

name: Account Dispute and Legal Hold Review
description: A review stage to identify any active disputes, legal holds, or outstanding fraud investigations associated with the account.
context: No legal holds (litigation, regulatory investigation, tax lien)

name: Account Verification Outcome Gate
description: A branching point where the process either proceeds if all checks are passed or triggers an escalation if issues are identified.

name: Issue Resolution and Documentation
description: The action of resolving identified account issues and recording the reason for any resulting delays in the system.

name: Manager
description: A supervisory role responsible for receiving escalations when account verification issues are identified.

name: Compliance Head
description: The head of the compliance department responsible for reviewing and resolving escalated account verification failures.

name: Level 1 — Management/Compliance Escalation
description: The first level of escalation triggered when verification issues are found, involving the Manager or Compliance Head.

name: Account Eligibility Compliance Check
description: A mandatory gate ensuring the account is free of legal holds, fraud investigations, and disputes before the process can advance.
context: No legal holds (litigation, regulatory investigation, tax lien)

name: Balance Calculation Process
description: An operational workflow used to determine the final balance of an account, involving transaction collection, balance calculation, documentation, and management approval. This process is part of the final stages of account closure.

name: Collect All Transactions Step
description: The initial stage of the balance calculation where all transactions since the last statement are gathered. This includes pending items such as standing orders and direct debits, and requires verification that no deposits or withdrawals remain unprocessed.
context: Pull all transactions since last statement
Include pending transactions (standing orders, direct debits due)

name: Calculate Final Balance Step
description: The stage where the final balance is computed using the ledger balance, adding pending interest and subtracting pending fees like overdrafts. The result must be verified against the account record in the Account Management System (AMS).
context: Add any pending interest (if accrual period not yet completed)
Subtract any pending fees (overdraft, if applicable)
Verify balance matches account record in AMS

name: Document Balance Step
description: The process of generating a formal final statement. This document must include the calculation date, a list of all pending transactions, and a clearly stated final balance.

name: Approval Step
description: The final quality control stage where an operations manager verifies the calculation, signs off on the statement, and files it within the account closure record.

name: Operations Manager
description: The individual responsible for the final verification of the balance calculation and the formal sign-off of the final statement.

name: Account Management System (AMS)
description: The system of record used to verify that the calculated balance matches the official account records.
context: Verify balance matches account record in AMS

name: Balance Verification Gate
description: A check to ensure that the manually calculated final balance matches the record stored in the AMS before proceeding to documentation.
context: Verify balance matches account record in AMS

name: Closing Account
description: The specific customer account being finalized and closed, for which the balance is being calculated and documented.
context: Verify balance matches account record in AMS

name: SmartSaver Account Closure Process
description: The operational workflow for closing a SmartSaver account, specifically involving the calculation of the final balance to remit by totaling the ledger balance and pending interest while subtracting pending fees.

name: SmartSaver Account
description: A specific bank account type undergoing the closure process, characterized by a ledger balance and pending interest calculations.

name: SmartSaver Product
description: The banking product associated with the account closure example provided in the calculation guide.

name: Final Balance Remittance Calculation
description: The step of determining the final payout amount by aggregating the Ledger Balance, adding Pending Interest, and deducting Pending Fees.

name: Account Closure Process
description: The overall operational workflow for closing a customer account, which includes the management and cancellation of recurring payments such as standing orders and direct debits.
context: Step 4: Process Standing Orders & Direct Debits

name: Standing Order Cancellation Step
description: A discrete action within the account closure process where all future standing orders are cancelled effectively immediately, with the exception of those scheduled before the closure date.
context: Cancel all future standing orders (effective immediately)
Last standing order executes if scheduled before closure date

name: Customer Cancellation Notification Step
description: The action of informing the customer that their standing orders have been cancelled as part of the account closure procedure.

name: Beneficiary Cancellation Notification Step
description: An optional action where the beneficiaries of the standing orders are notified that the payments have been cancelled.

name: Customer
description: The account holder who initiates the closure request and is the recipient of the cancellation notification.

name: Beneficiary
description: The recipient of a standing order who may optionally be notified of the payment cancellation.

name: Standing Order
description: Recurring payment instructions that must be cancelled immediately upon the account closure request, unless scheduled prior to the closure date.
context: Last standing order executes if scheduled before closure date

name: Direct Debit Cancellation Process
description: An operational workflow to cancel all Direct Debit mandates upon a closure request. The process is executed on the same day as the request and involves bank notification to billers.
context: Timeline: Same day as closure request

name: Direct Debit Mandate Cancellation
description: The action of cancelling all existing Direct Debit mandates, which becomes effective immediately upon execution.
context: Cancel all Direct Debit mandates (effective immediately)

name: Biller Notification
description: The bank's responsibility to notify the billers that the Direct Debit mandates have been cancelled.

name: Customer Cancellation Advice
description: The step where the customer is advised to independently confirm the cancellation with their billers.
context: Customer advised to confirm cancellation with billers separately

name: Bank Operational Staff
description: The entity responsible for the cancellation of mandates and the notification of billers.

name: Customer
description: The account holder who requests the closure and is responsible for ensuring billers receive the cancellation notice.
context: Customer advised to confirm cancellation with billers separately
Customer responsible for ensuring billers received cancellation notice

name: Transaction Processing Gate
description: A systemic block ensuring that no further Direct Debit transactions can be processed once the cancellation process is initiated.
context: No further DD transactions can be processed

name: Direct Debit Mandate
description: The specific financial authorization being cancelled as part of the account closure request.

name: Account Closure Process
description: The end-to-end operational workflow for closing a customer account. This specific section handles the assessment of the closure type and the standard path for customer-initiated requests.

name: Closure Type Assessment
description: The stage where the reason for account closure is evaluated to determine if it is a standard customer request or if regulatory/fraud concerns are present.

name: Closure Type Determination
description: A branching point to determine if the closure is a standard customer-initiated request without regulatory or fraud concerns. If conditions are met, the process proceeds to final payment.

name: Final Payment Processing
description: The action of processing the final payment for the account following a successful closure type assessment.

name: Closure Confirmation Issuance
description: The step of sending a standard confirmation notice to the customer once the closure process is complete.

name: Customer
description: The bank customer who voluntarily requests the closure of their account.

name: Closing Account
description: The specific bank account being subjected to the closure assessment and process.

name: Bank-Initiated Closure Process
description: A specialized operational workflow where the bank initiates the closure of an account due to regulatory, fraud, or policy reasons. The process may involve urgent freeze actions and requires specific approvals and notification periods ranging from immediate to 30 days.

name: Closure Reason Documentation
description: The action of recording the specific justification for the bank-initiated closure within the system.

name: Closure Approval Procurement
description: The stage where formal approval for the account closure is obtained from compliance or management.

name: Legal Review
description: A review conducted by the legal team specifically in cases where the closure is expected to have a significant financial impact.

name: Customer Notification
description: The process of notifying the customer of the closure, typically providing 30 days' notice, though this may be immediate in emergency scenarios.
context: Customer notice (30 days, or immediate if emergency)

name: Investigation Documentation Attachment
description: The finalization of the process by attaching all relevant investigation documentation to the account record.

name: Compliance Staff
description: Role responsible for providing approval for bank-initiated account closures.

name: Bank Manager
description: Role responsible for providing approval for bank-initiated account closures.

name: Legal Team
description: The team responsible for reviewing closures that may result in significant financial impact.

name: Financial Impact Assessment
description: A decision gate determining if the closure has a significant financial impact, which triggers a mandatory legal review.

name: Urgency/Emergency Determination
description: A decision point based on the nature of the closure (e.g., emergency vs standard) which determines whether the customer notice is immediate or 30 days.
context: Customer notice (30 days, or immediate if emergency)

name: Closure Approval Gate
description: The mandatory control point where approval from either compliance or a manager must be verified before the closure proceeds.

name: Frozen Account
description: An account that may be placed in a frozen state immediately during a bank-initiated closure process.

name: Affected Customer
description: The account holder who is the subject of the bank-initiated closure and must be notified.
context: Customer notice (30 days, or immediate if emergency)

name: Final Balance Payment Process
description: The final stage of a procedure focused on returning the remaining balance to a customer via four different disbursement methods: Bank Transfer, Check, Cash, or Hold for Instruction.

name: Bank Transfer Payment Execution
description: A preferred payment method where the customer provides receiving bank details and the transfer is initiated immediately via FPS, typically taking 1-2 business days.

name: Check Issuance and Mailing
description: The process of issuing a check in the customer's name and mailing it to their registered address, with a completion timeline of 3-5 business days.

name: Branch Cash Collection
description: Immediate payment provided at a branch where the customer collects cash and a teller issues a formal receipt.

name: Hold for Customer Instruction
description: The temporary holding of funds in a suspense account for up to 6 months while awaiting customer payment details, including a reminder at the 3-month mark.
context: Balance held in suspense account (maximum 6 months)
Customer instructed to provide payment details

name: Unclaimed Money Fund Transfer
description: The final action taken when funds held for customer instruction exceed the 6-month limit, resulting in a transfer to the unclaimed money fund.
context: Transferred to unclaimed money fund after 6 months

name: Customer
description: The recipient of the final balance who provides bank details, collects cash at the branch, or provides payment instructions.
context: Customer instructed to provide payment details

name: Branch Teller
description: The branch staff member responsible for issuing cash and providing the corresponding cash receipt.

name: Cash Limit Threshold Check
description: A decision gate based on the payment amount; if the amount is £5,000 or less, cash is permitted; if larger, check or transfer is recommended.
context: Larger amounts: Check or transfer recommended

name: Cash Payment Regulatory Limit
description: A mandatory regulatory control that limits cash disbursements to a maximum of £5,000.

name: Suspense Account
description: An internal account used to hold customer balances temporarily for up to 6 months pending payment instructions.
context: Balance held in suspense account (maximum 6 months)

name: Payment Processing
description: An operational workflow to handle the disbursement of payments to customers. The process involves confirming payment methods, collecting necessary details, and ensuring recording of the payment within a 5 business day timeline.

name: Payment Method Confirmation
description: The initial action where the operator verifies the preferred method of payment with the customer.

name: Payment Detail Acquisition
description: The step of collecting necessary routing information, specifically bank details for transfers or a physical address for checks.
context: Obtain bank details (if transfer) or address (if check)

name: Payment Execution
description: The operational act of processing the payment, which must be completed within a window of 5 business days.

name: Payment Sent Notification
description: The final communication step to inform the customer that the payment has been dispatched.

name: Payment System Recording
description: The final administrative action to record the payment in the system, marking the closure as complete.

name: Customer
description: The recipient of the payment who provides the payment method and necessary bank or address details.

name: Account Closure Process
description: The operational workflow for changing an account status from Active to Closed. This process involves system updates, recording closure details, and restricting all access and payments on the same day as the final payment.
context: Timeline: Same day as final payment

name: Account Status Update
description: The technical action of updating the account status to 'Closed' and recording the closure date and reason. It also involves recording the final balance.

name: Payment Instruction Cancellation
description: The step where all active standing orders and Direct Debits associated with the account are marked as cancelled and blocked.

name: Access Restriction Enforcement
description: The process of disabling online banking access, deactivating issued cards, and prohibiting new transactions.

name: Fraud Detection Engine
description: An automated system that monitors accounts for fraudulent activity and must be updated to exclude the account once it is closed.
context: Fraud detection: Account excluded from monitoring

name: Closing Account
description: The specific customer account undergoing the status change from Active to Closed.
context: Customer profile: Account marked as closed

name: Cancelled Standing Orders
description: Standing order instructions that are terminated as part of the account closure procedure.

name: Cancelled Direct Debits
description: Direct Debit mandates that are terminated and blocked during the account closure process.

name: Deactivated Account Card
description: The payment card associated with the account which is automatically deactivated upon closure.

name: Account Closure Process
description: The operational workflow for closing a customer account, including the final notification requirements and records retention obligations.

name: Customer Notification Step
description: The final stage of the closure process where the bank sends a confirmation letter to the customer via email and postal mail within 2 business days of closure.
context: Sent within 2 business days of closure

name: Bank Operations Staff
description: The internal bank actor responsible for generating and delivering the Closure Confirmation Letter to the customer.
context: Delivery: Email (if email on file), Postal mail (required, to registered address)

name: Closing Customer
description: The customer whose account is being closed and who receives the confirmation notification.
context: Sent within 2 business days of closure

name: Closing Account
description: The specific customer account being closed, identified by account number and product name in the confirmation letter.

name: Standing Order Cancellation
description: The action of cancelling standing orders associated with the closed account, which must be confirmed in the notification letter.

name: Direct Debit Cancellation
description: The action of cancelling direct debit mandates associated with the closed account, which must be confirmed in the notification letter.

name: Records Retention Compliance Check
description: A regulatory requirement to notify the customer that account records will be archived for a period of 6 years.

name: Account Closure Record Retention and Archive Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for archiving account closing documentation and transaction records. It specifies a 6-year retention period in accordance with POCA and AML Regulations, ending in secure destruction.
context: Retention Period: 6 years from closure date (per POCA, AML Regulations)
Destruction Procedure: At 6-year mark: Schedule for secure destruction

name: Document Archival
description: The action of storing specific account opening, transaction, and closure documents within a secure document management system. This ensures all regulatory evidence is preserved for the mandatory period.
context: Records to Archive (6 Years): Account opening documents (KYC, ID, address verification)
Storage Location: Secure document management system (DMS)

name: Secure Destruction Procedure
description: The final stage of the retention lifecycle occurring at the 6-year mark. It involves shredding paper, deleting digital records, and obtaining a formal certificate of destruction.
context: Destruction Procedure: At 6-year mark: Schedule for secure destruction

name: Secure Document Management System
description: The encrypted and access-controlled system responsible for storing archived records and maintaining an audit trail of all access.
context: Storage Location: Secure document management system (DMS)

name: POCA and AML Regulatory Retention Check
description: A mandatory regulatory gate ensuring that all required documentation is retained for exactly 6 years from the closure date as per Proceeds of Crime Act (POCA) and AML Regulations.
context: Retention Period: 6 years from closure date (per POCA, AML Regulations)

name: Closing Account
description: The specific bank account being closed, for which records including the closure request, reason, and final statement must be archived.

name: Standard Customer-Initiated Closure Process
description: An end-to-end operational workflow for closing a SmartSaver Account initiated by a customer via telephone. The process involves balance calculation, fund transfer via FPS, and formal confirmation, completing within a 3-day timeline.
context: Result: ✅ Closed in 3 days, customer satisfied

name: Closure Request Initiation
description: The initial stage where the customer contacts the bank via phone to request account closure, provides receiving bank details, and the request is logged in the system.
context: Requests closure, all balance to bank transfer

name: Closure Processing and Payment Initiation
description: The operational stage where the final balance is calculated, a payment is initiated via Faster Payments Service (FPS), and a confirmation letter is generated.

name: Account Finalisation and Archiving
description: The final stage where the customer receives funds and confirmation, the account status is formally updated to 'Closed', and records are archived.

name: Customer
description: The bank customer who initiates the closure request of their SmartSaver Account via the designated phone line.
context: Requests closure, all balance to bank transfer

name: Operations Team
description: The internal banking team responsible for processing the closure request, calculating balances, and initiating the transfer of funds.

name: Banking System
description: The automated system used to note closure requests and update account statuses to 'Closed'.

name: SmartSaver Account
description: The specific customer account being closed during this operational scenario.

name: SmartSaver Product
description: The banking product type associated with the account being closed.

name: Closure Balance Transfer
description: The final financial event where the calculated balance of the account is transferred to the customer's external bank via FPS.

name: Bank-Initiated Account Closure (Policy Violation)
description: An operational workflow for closing a customer account initiated by the bank due to policy violations, specifically suspected unauthorized use. The process involves a fraud hold, investigation, refunding unauthorized transactions, and a mandatory 30-day notice period before final closure.
context: Customer: Suspected unauthorized use, investigation underway

name: Immediate Account Freeze
description: The first action taken on Day 1 where the account is frozen immediately via a fraud hold to prevent further unauthorized activity.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: The internal banking team responsible for initiating and completing the investigation into suspected unauthorized account use.
context: Investigation initiated by Financial Crime team

name: Investigation Initiation
description: The formal start of the investigation into the account's activity by the Financial Crime team.
context: Investigation initiated by Financial Crime team

name: Customer Freeze Notification
description: Notifying the customer that their account has been frozen. Crucially, no reason is disclosed at this stage to avoid tipping off risk.
context: Customer notified of freeze (no reason disclosed—tipping off risk)

name: Investigation Completion and Transaction Confirmation
description: The phase between Day 2 and Day 7 where the investigation is finalized and unauthorized transactions are officially confirmed.

name: Refund Processing
description: The step of processing refunds to the customer for the transactions confirmed as unauthorized during the investigation.

name: Account Closure Decision
description: A decision point occurring between Day 2 and Day 7 where the bank determines that the account must be closed due to the policy violation.

name: Policy Violation Closure Notice
description: Sending the formal notice to the customer on Day 8 stating the account will be closed due to policy violation and triggering the 30-day notice period.
context: Notice sent to customer: "Account closure due to policy violation"

name: Final Balance Transfer
description: The action on Day 38 to transfer the remaining final balance to the customer, deducting any applicable chargebacks.

name: Official Account Closure
description: The final administrative step on Day 38 to officially close the account after the 30-day notice period has elapsed.

name: Records Archiving
description: The final step of the process where records related to the policy violation and closure are archived.

name: Affected Customer
description: The bank customer whose account is subject to investigation for unauthorized use and subsequent policy-driven closure.
context: Customer: Suspected unauthorized use, investigation underway

name: Frozen/Closing Account
description: The specific customer account that is frozen on Day 1 and officially closed on Day 38 following a policy violation.

name: Unauthorized Transactions
description: Financial events on the account that were investigated and confirmed as unauthorized, leading to refunds.

name: Account Closure Quality Assurance Process
description: An operational workflow designed to ensure that account closures are executed accurately and in compliance with banking standards. It consists of a pre-closure checklist and a monthly audit cycle for file review.

name: Closure Request Documentation
description: The initial step of ensuring that the formal request to close the account has been properly recorded and documented before proceeding.

name: Customer Identity Verification
description: A security step to verify the identity of the customer making the closure request to prevent unauthorized account termination.

name: Final Balance Calculation
description: The process of accurately calculating the final remaining balance in the account prior to closure.

name: Standing Order and Direct Debit Cancellation
description: The step of ensuring all active standing orders and direct debit mandates associated with the account are terminated.

name: Final Payment Initiation
description: The action of initiating the final transfer of funds to the customer to clear the account balance.

name: Customer Closure Confirmation
description: The formal step of notifying the customer that their account has been successfully closed.

name: System Account Status Update
description: Updating the core banking system to reflect the changed status of the account from active to closed.

name: Records Archival Flagging
description: The process of flagging the account records for a mandatory 6-year archival period for regulatory compliance.

name: Monthly Closure File Review
description: A periodic quality assurance step where at least 5 closure files are reviewed monthly to ensure completeness, accuracy, and timeline adherence.

name: Closure Compliance Review
description: A formal assessment during the monthly audit to identify any compliance issues related to the account closure process.

name: Account Re-opening Process
description: The procedure followed when a customer requests to re-open an account after a closure request, requiring a full KYC cycle.

name: Account Closure Exception Handling
description: Operational workflow for resolving common issues encountered during the account closure process, including standing order timing and disputes.
context: Pending standing order on closure date

name: Full KYC Verification
description: The requirement to perform a complete Know Your Customer verification process when an account needs to be re-opened.

name: Final Standing Order Execution
description: The action of executing the final remaining standing order before proceeding with the account closure to resolve timing issues.

name: Closure Dispute Investigation
description: The process of reopening an investigation into a customer claim received after an account has already been closed.
context: Reopen investigation, may reverse closure if warranted

name: Uncollected Check Holding Period
description: A holding period of 6 months for checks not collected by the customer before they are escalated to unclaimed money procedures.
context: Hold 6 months, escalate to unclaimed money procedures

name: Closure Reversal Decision
description: A decision point following a dispute investigation to determine if a closed account should be reversed/re-opened based on the warrants of the claim.

name: Unclaimed Money Procedures Escalation
description: The escalation tier reached when a customer fails to collect a payment check after a 6-month holding period.

name: Customer
description: The individual requesting account re-opening, disputing a closure, or failing to collect payment checks.

name: Closing Account
description: The bank account currently undergoing the closure process or recently closed, which may be subject to disputes or standing order executions.
context: Pending standing order on closure date

name: Pending Standing Order
description: A standing order that remains active on the date of account closure and must be executed before final closure.
context: Pending standing order on closure date

name: Full KYC Compliance Check
description: A mandatory compliance gate requiring full KYC verification to be satisfied before a requested account re-opening can proceed.

name: Account Closure Process
description: The operational procedure for closing a bank account. This process is the reverse of the account opening procedure and is distinct from the Account Dormancy SOP.

name: Account Opening Process
description: The procedure for opening a new account, referenced as the reverse process of account closure.

name: Account Dormancy Procedure
description: A specific operational procedure dealing with dormant accounts, explicitly noted as being different from the account closure process.

name: Record Retention Process
description: The policy and procedure for archiving records, specifying a 6-year archive period.

name: Head of Operations
description: The individual responsible for authoring and updating the operational procedure documents, including versions 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2.

name: Head of Operations
description: A senior executive responsible for the final sign-off and approval of the operational procedure document.
context: Approved by: Head of Operations — Date: 2026-01-15

name: Head of Retail Banking
description: A senior executive responsible for the final sign-off and approval of the operational procedure document.
context: Approved by: Head of Retail Banking — Date: 2026-01-15

name: Chief Operating Officer
description: The highest level of operational authority responsible for the final sign-off and approval of the operational procedure document.
